stops.name: The Nile, among the flags: the basket of bulrushes
stops.campa: Pharaoh has decreed every Hebrew son cast into the river. A daughter of Levi hides her boy three months, then daubs an ark of bulrushes with slime and pitch and lays it among the reeds at the river's brink. His sister stands afar to watch. Pharaoh's daughter comes down to bathe; she sees the ark, hears the child weep, and has compassion. "This is one of the Hebrews' children," she says. The sister runs and fetches the child's own mother to nurse him for wages. The river that was to drown him carries him instead into the palace.
stops.quote: And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.

stops.name: The court of Pharaoh at Pi-Ramesses (Qantir)
stops.campa: Grown in the house of Pharaoh's daughter, Moses is a prince of Egypt, learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, yet the milk of a Hebrew mother is in him. The aggadah tells how as a child he took the crown from Pharaoh's head, and an angel guided his hand to a coal, so that ever after his speech was slow and his tongue heavy. He walks the granite halls of the delta capital of Rameses, a Levite disguised as an heir, and the burden of his people begins to weigh on him.

stops.name: Goshen: the Egyptian slain
stops.campa: Moses goes out to his brethren and looks on their burdens. He sees an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew, one of his own. He looks this way and that, and seeing no man, he strikes the Egyptian down and hides him in the sand. The next day he finds two Hebrews striving, and reproves the wrongdoer, who answers: "Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me?" So the deed is known. Pharaoh hears, and seeks to slay Moses. The prince becomes a fugitive.
stops.quote: Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian?

stops.name: The well of Midian at Al-Bad' (Madyan)
stops.campa: Moses flees eastward, out of Egypt, over the wilderness to the land of Midian, and sits down by a well. The seven daughters of the priest of Midian come to draw water and fill the troughs for their father's flock, but the shepherds drive them away. Moses stands up and helps them, and waters their flock. Their father Reuel, called Jethro, marvels they are come so soon. "An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds," they say. He calls the stranger in to bread.
stops.quote: And when the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.

stops.name: Midian, the house of Jethro; Zipporah
stops.campa: Moses is content to dwell with the man, who gives him Zipporah his daughter to wife. She bears a son, and he calls him Gershom, for he says, "I have been a stranger in a strange land." Forty years the prince becomes a shepherd, keeping the flock of Jethro the priest, learning the desert and its silences. In Egypt the king who sought his life dies; the children of Israel sigh under their bondage, and their cry comes up unto God. God remembers His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
stops.quote: I have been a stranger in a strange land.

stops.name: Horeb, the burning bush
stops.campa: Leading the flock to the backside of the desert, Moses comes to Horeb, the mountain of God. The angel of the LORD appears in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush; the bush burns and is not consumed. He turns aside to see this great sight, and God calls to him out of the bush: "Moses, Moses." "Here am I." "Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground." And He declares Himself the God of the fathers, come down to deliver Israel. Moses hides his face, afraid to look upon God.
stops.quote: Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

stops.name: Horeb: I AM THAT I AM, the rod and the leprous hand
stops.campa: Moses asks the Name. God answers: "I AM THAT I AM," and bids him say to Israel, I AM hath sent me. To arm his mouth against unbelief, God gives him signs. The rod cast down becomes a serpent, and Moses flees from it; taken by the tail, it is a rod again. His hand thrust into his bosom comes out leprous, white as snow; put in again, it is restored. Still Moses pleads he is slow of speech; God appoints Aaron his brother to be his mouth, and sends him back to Egypt. The bush has spoken; the exile is over.
stops.quote: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.

stops.name: The inn on the way, the bridegroom of blood
stops.campa: On the road back to Egypt, at a lodging place, the LORD meets Moses and seeks to kill him, for his son is uncircumcised. Zipporah takes a sharp stone, cuts off her son's foreskin, and casts it at Moses' feet. "Surely a bloody husband art thou to me." So the LORD lets him go. It is a dark and terrible mercy on the threshold of the mission: the deliverer must himself be marked with the covenant of Abraham before he can carry it to Pharaoh.
stops.quote: Surely a bloody husband art thou to me.

stops.name: The court of Pharaoh: let my people go
stops.campa: Aaron meets Moses at the mount of God and kisses him; together they gather the elders of Israel, and Aaron does the signs, and the people believe and bow their heads. Then Moses and Aaron stand before Pharaoh: "Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go." Pharaoh answers, "Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice? I know not the LORD." He lays heavier labour on them, straw no longer given, bricks still demanded. Aaron casts down his rod; it becomes a serpent and swallows the rods of the magicians. Pharaoh's heart is hardened.
stops.quote: Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.

stops.name: The Nile turned to blood: the first plague
stops.campa: Moses meets Pharaoh at the water's brink in the morning and lifts the rod. All the waters of the Nile turn to blood; the fish die, the river stinks, and Egypt cannot drink. Seven days the blood endures. So begin the wonders in the land of Ham. The magicians ape the sign with their enchantments, and Pharaoh's heart stays hard; he turns and goes into his house, and sets not his heart to this also. The god-river of Egypt bleeds, and its people dig about the banks for water.
stops.quote: And all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.

stops.name: Frogs, lice, flies: plagues two, three, four
stops.campa: The river brings forth frogs abundantly; they cover the land, come into the houses, the bedchambers, the ovens, the kneading-troughs. Pharaoh begs relief, then hardens. Aaron smites the dust and it becomes lice in man and beast; the magicians cannot do so and confess, "This is the finger of God." Then swarms of flies fill the houses of Egypt, but in Goshen where Israel dwells there is no swarm, that Pharaoh may know the LORD is in the midst of the earth. Between plagues the king relents, and relenting, hardens again.
stops.quote: Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God.

stops.name: Murrain, boils, hail: plagues five, six, seven
stops.campa: A grievous murrain falls on the cattle of the Egyptians, and all die, but of Israel's cattle not one. Moses casts ashes of the furnace toward heaven, and boils break forth on man and beast, so the magicians cannot stand before him. Then Moses stretches the rod, and the LORD sends thunder and hail, fire running along the ground, the worst in all the land of Egypt; the hail smites herb and tree and breaks them. Only in Goshen there is no hail. Pharaoh cries, "I have sinned," and hardens once the storm is stayed.
stops.quote: The LORD sent thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground.
